question: (i) Obtain the expression for the electric potential due to an electric dipole at a distant point. (ii) Hence find the electric field on the axial line of the dipole using the potential expression.

options.A: For a short dipole at a distant point, $V=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{p\cos\theta}{r^2}$. On the axial line, $V=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{p}{r^2}$. Hence $E=-\dfrac{dV}{dr}=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{2p}{r^3}$.
options.D: Dipole potential is constant at all distant points, so axial field is zero.
